title: Two Footlockers Of Fossils Left Beijing And Never Arrived

basis.note: median of recent videos blended with the niche benchmark; learning gated until day 5

segments.narration: Two crates of human fossils left Beijing and vanished. Inside were bones from at least forty individuals, dug out of a place called Dragon Bone Hill.
Zhoukoudian had produced the best early-human collection on earth. In 1941, with Japan closing in, China sent it to New York for safekeeping.
US Marines were to load the footlockers onto the liner President Harrison. The ship never made port. Japanese warships attacked it and ran it aground.
They left the medical college on the fourth of December, 1941, and were never reliably seen again. Sunk at sea? Ground up for medicine?
One marine said he dug up a box of bones at Qinhuangdao in 1947. A port researcher reckons the likely spot is under a parking lot.

verdicts.claim: US Marines were to carry the footlockers to the SS President Harrison at Qinhuangdao, but Japanese warships attacked the ship and it ran aground before reaching port.

verdicts.claim: The fossils left the Peking Union Medical College on 4 December 1941 and their whereabouts since are unknown; theories include loss aboard a sunken ship and being ground up for medicine.

verdicts.claim: Marine Richard Bowen said he dug up a box of bones at Qinhuangdao in 1947, and a Chinese port researcher said the most probable location would be under roads, a warehouse or a parking lot.

candidates.why: Two countable objects, a departure and no arrival, with the loop built in.

candidates.text: Bones from forty ancient humans went missing in days
candidates.why: Stronger number, but 'went missing' is vaguer than crates leaving a city.

candidates.text: A marine dug up a box of bones in 1947
candidates.why: The best lead in the case, but meaningless before the loss is established.

choice.reason: It is the most concrete version, two boxes you can picture, and it sets the departure and the disappearance in a single breath.
